title: Assembly of projective normal component models and Cartier markings
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $T$ be a nonempty reduced proper finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and enumerate its distinct reduced irreducible components $T_1,\ldots,T_s$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion], where $1\le s<\infty$. Let $C\subseteq T$ be closed and nowhere dense. For each $i$ suppose $N_i$ is a nonempty integral normal geometrically reduced $e$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], where normal means every local ring is an integrally closed domain, with a closed immersion $N_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{m_i}_e$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Suppose $q_i:N_i\to T_i$ is a proper $e$-morphism, surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and birational (an isomorphism between dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]), and $\mathcal J_i$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] on $N_i$ with support $q_i^{-1}(C\cap T_i)$. Then the scheme disjoint union $B=\coprod_{i=1}^sN_i$ and induced $e$-morphism $q:B\to T$ exist. Each $N_i$ is an open-and-closed subscheme of $B$. The scheme $B$ is proper and finite type over $e$, geometrically reduced, and admits a closed immersion $B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^M_e$, with $M+1=\sum_i(m_i+1)$ [def-kun-projective]. The ideals $\mathcal J_i$ are restrictions of an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal J$ on $B$, with support $q^{-1}C$. The morphism $q$ is surjective, maps the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of each $N_i$ to the generic point of $T_i$, and induces isomorphisms of the corresponding residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus it induces a bijection between the component generic points of $B$ and $T$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150: reconstruction from the finitely many components. Agent expansion of the finite disjoint union using disjoint projective coordinate blocks and Cartier ideals on open-and-closed summands.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to the finite family $(N_i)$. It gives $B$, its pairwise disjoint clopen summands, and a unique $e$-morphism $q:B\to T$ whose restriction to $N_i$ is $N_i\xrightarrow{q_i}T_i\hookrightarrow T$. For $t\in T$, choose $i$ with $t\in T_i$ and then $n\in N_i$ with $q_i(n)=t$. Thus $q$ is surjective.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); ILO X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150

proof.text: Write $a_i:N_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{m_i}_e$ for the given embeddings and $L_i=a_i^*\mathcal O(1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], the sections $a_i^*T_{i,a}$ locally freely generate $L_i$, and at every point at least one is nonzero. On a disjoint open cover sheaves are given componentwise: put $L(U)=\prod_i L_i(U\cap N_i)$ with componentwise restrictions and $\mathcal O_B(U)$-action. The sheaf axiom follows by gluing separately in each $N_i$, and [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies its restriction with $L_i$. Hence $L$ is invertible. For each $(i,a)$ let $s_{i,a}$ restrict to $a_i^*T_{i,a}$ on $N_i$ and to zero elsewhere. These sections generate $L$ at every point. Order their $\sum_i(m_i+1)=M+1$ indices. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] and the base-change construction [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] to obtain an $e$-morphism $a:B\to\mathbf P^M_e$.

For the standard target chart $D_+(T_{i,a})$, [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage] identifies its inverse image with $W_{i,a}=a_i^{-1}(D_+(T_{i,a}))\subset N_i$: the section $s_{i,a}$ is zero on every other summand. The chart description [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] and the affine quotient criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] give $W_{i,a}=\operatorname{Spec}(e[u_b:b\ne a]/K_{i,a})$, where $u_b=T_{i,b}/T_{i,a}$ in the original projective space. By the ratio formula in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage], the ring map for $a$ on this chart sends $T_{i,b}/T_{i,a}$ to $u_b\bmod K_{i,a}$ and $T_{j,c}/T_{i,a}$ to zero for $j\ne i$. It is surjective since the $u_b$ generate the quotient. Thus every chart restriction of $a$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. These standard target charts cover; apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-finite-etale-zariski-local] to conclude that $a$ is a closed immersion. This proves the specified dimension bound, without changing any of the given embeddings.

source.place: Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); morphisms.tex Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine quotient criterion; agent block-coordinate calculation

proof.text: The closed immersion $a$ makes $B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ projective in [def-kun-projective]. By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] this morphism is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01W1 (definition-proper); Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), applied to an H-projective morphism

proof.text: For every field extension $E/e$, [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] identifies $B_E$ with $\coprod_i(N_i)_E$, with the indicated coprojections and projections. At any point its local ring is that of its summand by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Each such local ring is reduced, since each $N_i$ is geometrically reduced. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $B_E$ is reduced for every $E$, so $B$ is geometrically reduced.

source.place: Tags 01JB and 01JC, empty-overlap gluing and its base change; reducedness checked on the displayed local rings

proof.text: On an open $U\subset B$ define $\mathcal J(U)=\prod_i\mathcal J_i(U\cap N_i)\subset\prod_i\mathcal O_{N_i}(U\cap N_i)=\mathcal O_B(U)$, with componentwise restriction. Gluing sections separately on each summand verifies the sheaf axiom. By [def-weil-open-immersion], its restriction to $N_i$ is exactly $\mathcal J_i$. Its quasi-coherent affine presentations and local generators are those of $\mathcal J_i$ on the affine open covers inside $N_i$; these form an open cover of $B$. Their generators remain non-zero-divisors in the same rings, so [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] makes $\mathcal J$ effective Cartier. Here support means the support of $\mathcal O_B/\mathcal J$. On each summand it is $q_i^{-1}(C\cap T_i)$, which equals $(q^{-1}C)\cap N_i$, proving the asserted support equality.

source.place: Tags 01WR (definition-effective-Cartier-divisor), 01WS (lemma-characterize-effective-Cartier-divisor), local non-zero-divisor formulation; agent explicit product-of-sections construction

proof.text: By [def-pc-integral-scheme] each $N_i$ is irreducible, and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] supplies its unique generic point $\eta_i$ and that of each $T_i$. Choose the dense open isomorphism $U_i\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i$ defining birationality of $q_i$. A generic point belongs to every nonempty open: otherwise its closure lies in the complementary closed subset. Thus $\eta_i\in U_i$. Its image is generic in $V_i$, hence generic in $T_i$ since $V_i$ is dense. These are exactly the generic points of the distinct components of $T$. An irreducible subset of $B$ cannot meet two clopen summands, since that would split it into two disjoint nonempty open subsets; therefore the $N_i$ are exactly the irreducible components of $B$. For residue fields, the open inclusions $U_i\hookrightarrow N_i$, $V_i\hookrightarrow T_i$ induce isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], and the displayed isomorphism induces an isomorphism on residue fields. The inclusions $T_i\hookrightarrow T$ induce isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso]; the clopen inclusions $N_i\hookrightarrow B$ do so by the open-immersion case. The composite maps are the maps induced by $q$. This proves both the asserted residue-field isomorphisms and the bijection on component generic points.

Each chart restriction is therefore a closed immersion, and Zariski-locality clause (1) makes a a closed immersion.
